question:

Where have all the honey bees gone? It is really hard to see them these days. About one third of the bee population dies every year. The bees are disappearing! This is bad news for bees, but it's even worse news for people.

Bees are very helpful to humans. First, bees give honey to us. Honey is a truly wonderful food. It is good for our health and tastes great. Honey can last almost forever. In fact, honey from ancient Egypt can be eaten today! Second, bees help produce many crops such as apples and strawberries. These crops cannot be produced by themselves. They need the help of bees. Bees help in the process of pollination.

When bees gather nectar from flowers, they transfer pollen from the male parts of one flowers to the female parts of another flowers and this allows the flower to produce fruit or seeds. This is called pollination.

- What is pollen?
It is a fine yellow powder produced by flowers.

Why are bees disappearing? One of the reasons is climate change. Global warming has brought extremely hot and cold weather. Bees cannot survive in these conditions. Another reason is the harmful chemicals farmers use on crops. These chemicals kill good insects like bees as well as bad insects.

Then what can we do to help our little yellow friends? First, we can plant more flowers and trees. This will provide a good environment for bees to live in. Also, trees help slows down global warming. Second, the use of harmful chemicals on crops must be stopped right away. These chemicals are unhealthy for bees and people. Our little friends need our help. Let's not let them down!
